strategies.name: fvg_trend_continuation_entry
strategies.description: an imbalance in the market where price moved so aggressively in one direction that it left a gap between candles without proper trading activity

entry_sequence.action: the gap you know is created between three candlesticks
So the gap from the closing point of the first candle to the opening point of the third candle. So the gap in between is what is called an imbalance

this is an example of a bearish imbalance just same thing with you know the explanation for the bullish imbalance. So make sure structure is present and then you look out for the you know first three candles and um you map it out from the closing points when it's a sell. You can see it's from the closing point of the first candle and also the opening point of the third candle
patiently wait for you know price to get there tap in
wait for price to tap in and then push to your direction

confluences.description: the probability of your treads playing out when you are sticking to the trend is higher than when you are going against the trend
the imbalance must create a break of structure
don't just you know map out any FVG on the chart map out the FVG that cost the break of structure
there should also be liquidity price will clear before you know tapping into the imbalance
map out the FVG that is very close to the order block

stop.description: put your stop loss a little bit below the fair value gap
stop.buy_rule: stop loss a little bit ... below if you are buying
stop.sell_rule: stop loss a little bit above if you're selling
stop.constraint: you will now drag the stop loss to also accommodate the other block that will you know kill the um risk-to-reward ratio of the tread ... Just stick to the fair value gap
